about: Every capability a harness test may prove (contract harness, 3.1 `proves`). The status page is generated from this list and the results that name each id (plan rule 8). An id is added with the task that builds it; it is never renamed or reused.

capabilities.sound.effect: A sound effect (assets/<path>.sound.json naming a WAV, FLAC or Ogg Vorbis file beside it: volume, pitch range, distances, priority, bus, positioned, loop) becomes Luma/<id>/<path>.nsfx, 48 kHz 16-bit with its loop sample-exact and its EBU R 128 loudness measured; a file of another kind, too many channels, a rate out of range, a loop outside the sound and every wrong value are refused by name (3.7 layer 1)
capabilities.sound.replace: A mod's sound effect with "replace": "<name>" keeps the game sound's name for the audio service to play it in that sound's place; the name is checked against the game's 3,487 sound names and refused by name when the game lacks it (3.7 layer 2)
capabilities.layout.cook: A screen layout (<Name>.arc/<Name>.layout.json: panes, pictures with the archive's timg/ textures and corner colours, text in the game's fonts, bounding panes, groups) becomes the archive's blyt/<Name>.brlyt, which the store cooks and the game's layout loader reads as its own; a texture the mod lacks, a name twice, text past its length and every wrong value are refused by name (3.8 layer 1)
capabilities.anim.replace: An animation file (<archive>.arc/<any>.anim.glb, joints only) makes clips of the archive's game model by name, replacing the game's clip of that name; a channel on no joint, a joint hung elsewhere than in the game's model, a key that is no number or a clip past 65,535 frames is refused by name (3.6 layer 2)
capabilities.anim.events: A clip's frame events (<archive>.arc/<clip>.anim.json: frame and event name) become <clip>.events beside the clip, sorted by frame, for the anim service's plays; a frame past the game clip's last, a name not 1-63 of A-Z a-z 0-9 _ ., an event twice at one frame or more than 64 are refused by name (3.6 layer 3)
capabilities.stage.args: A stage table row of jmp/ (whole, merge/ or a patch by key) gives its object's arguments by name ("args": {"ShotInterval": 120}): the names are the fields each MR::getPlacementArg call of the object's class and bases fills, from the game's luma-placement.json; they become Obj_arg0-7 (-1 where not given, true 1, false and null -1); an unknown object, an unknown name or an argument given twice is refused by name (3.9 layer 1)
capabilities.harness.self: A check of the harness itself, or a fixture: proves nothing about LumaCore
capabilities.kernel.bind: A mod's library is bound by name before its first line runs: every import or none, a missing name refused with a message naming it (0.2, 1.1)
capabilities.kernel.call: A mod calls any function of the game by name and signature (0.2, 1.1)
capabilities.kernel.field: A mod reads and writes any field of the game's types by Class.field and type (0.2, 1.2)
capabilities.kernel.global: A mod reads and writes any global the game defines, by its qualified name and type (1.2)
capabilities.kernel.type: A mod knows the size of any record of the game by its name or an alias's (1.2)
capabilities.kernel.hook.before: A before hook on any function: runs first, may skip the function (0.2, 1.1)
capabilities.kernel.hook.after: An after hook on any function: runs last, may change the result (0.2, 1.1)
capabilities.kernel.hook.wrap: A wrap on any function: runs around it and calls proceed (0.2, 1.1)
capabilities.kernel.hook.replace: A replace on any function: one mod holds it, a second is refused naming the first (0.2, 1.1)
capabilities.format.code: A mod's code is found at code/<platform>/mod.<ending> by luma.json code.platforms alone; a mod with none for this device is off with the reason (luma-format 6)
capabilities.kernel.refusal: Every refusal to load a mod names its cause in the log and on the Mods screen (0.2 Z-1, 1.1)
capabilities.kernel.service: A mod finds a service by name and version through LumaCore.service (0.3, 2.x)
capabilities.kernel.memory: Memory for a mod from LumaCore.alloc: aligned up to 65536, counted per mod, null when there is none, freed when the mod is taken out (1.1)
capabilities.kernel.report: A mod's runtime reports an error by code: said once in English with its place, kept for the Mods page in the player's language, repeats counted (1.1)
capabilities.kernel.unhook: Hooks added and taken out while the game runs: a call already running keeps its hooks (1.1)
capabilities.kernel.threads: A hook runs on its caller's thread and knows whether it is the game thread; hook and unhook only from the game thread (1.1)
capabilities.kernel.released: A mod's handles to objects are emptied when their memory goes (lumacore::released) (1.1)
capabilities.kernel.cxx: A mod written in C++: globals built before start in order, new and delete on the mod's memory, destructors at its end (1.1)
capabilities.kernel.bind.method: A virtual is bound by name and signature as one function that runs the object's own class's override (kind 8, LUMA_METHOD; 1.3)
capabilities.kernel.objects.own_class: A mod asks any game object its own class: the class's number, from the object's run-time type (1.3)
capabilities.kernel.objects.number: A class's number is the same in the module, the types file and class_of: the record's index among the records sorted by name (1.3)
capabilities.kernel.objects.as_class: A mod turns an object pointer into a pointer to any of its classes, bases included, or null when it is not one (1.3)
capabilities.kernel.objects.is_a: A mod asks whether an object is of a class, its own or a base (1.3)
capabilities.kernel.objects.method: A mod finds a virtual by name and signature and calls it on any object, the object's own override running with its hooks (1.3)
capabilities.kernel.objects.overrider: A mod asks which function overrides a virtual for an object, as that function's row (1.3)
capabilities.kernel.objects.call_method: A mod calls a virtual on an object by name and signature in one call, the object adjusted to the declaring class (1.3)
capabilities.kernel.classes.define: A mod defines a class of its own from a game class: its name, base, maker, data and overrides; its number known to class_of (1.4)
capabilities.kernel.classes.made: The game's own factory makes a mod class's objects where a stage places its name or the name it replaces, through the base's maker (1.4)
capabilities.kernel.classes.data: Each object of a mod class has its own data, zeroed, found from the object (1.4)
capabilities.kernel.classes.override: A mod class's override runs for its own objects only; every other object runs the game's function (1.4)
capabilities.kernel.classes.objects: own_class, as_class and is_a answer for a mod class's objects: the mod class, and every class of its base (1.4)
capabilities.kernel.classes.refusals: define_class refuses each kind of wrong definition with its number and words, leaving nothing of it (1.4)
capabilities.kernel.classes.taken_out: A mod taken out ends its classes; their objects are the game's own again and the game goes on (1.4, 1.11)
capabilities.kernel.classes.scene: A new scene makes a mod class's objects again; the old scene's are forgotten with it (1.4)
capabilities.kernel.guard.resume: A fault in a mod's code (an access it may not make, an illegal instruction, a division by zero) is caught at the boundary: the game goes on as if the code did nothing, the mod is off and taken out, the player told on screen and in the mod log (1.6)
capabilities.kernel.guard.boundaries: Every place the kernel runs a mod's code is a boundary: before, after, wrap and replace hooks, start, stop, a service's event, a class's made and override (1.6)
capabilities.kernel.guard.nested: Boundaries nest per thread: a mod's hook calls the game, whose function another mod hooks; a fault names the innermost mod, the outer goes on (1.6)
capabilities.kernel.guard.not_resumed: A stack overflow, or a fault in the game's code under a mod's call, is not resumed: the game ends with a report naming the mod, never silently (1.6)
capabilities.kernel.guard.cost: No mod: no boundary runs and nothing is measured; with a mod, a boundary's cost against a plain call is measured in a harness run (1.6)
capabilities.kernel.guard.time: Each mod's code time per frame (its boundaries' own time, less the nested ones), the average and the worst of its last 120 frames, read from any thread by luma_guard_cost (1.6)
capabilities.kernel.reload.take_out: A mod taken out while the game runs: its hooks go, its stop runs, dependents first, what it held counted and freed (1.11)
capabilities.kernel.numbers.by_name: Every number the game reads in a function's code, by the function's name, signature and place, and every file's number constant by its name: address and kind (1.5)
capabilities.kernel.numbers.set: A mod sets one by name and the game's code reads the new value (1.5)
capabilities.kernel.numbers.refusals: No such number, several, a value not of its kind: refused with its number and words (1.5)
capabilities.kernel.numbers.taken_out: A mod taken out: every number it set is the game's again, or what the mods still here set last (1.5, 1.11)
capabilities.kernel.tables.by_name: Every file-scope or class-static table of the game's data (an array or plain record with an initializer) by its name: data, element type, size, count (1.5)
capabilities.kernel.tables.set: A mod writes bytes in a table by name and the game reads them (1.5)
capabilities.kernel.tables.refusals: No such table, bytes outside it, off the game thread: refused with the table's name and words (1.5)
capabilities.kernel.tables.taken_out: A mod taken out: every table it wrote is the game's again with the writes of the mods still here, in order (1.5, 1.11)
capabilities.kernel.objects.unit: Classes a .cpp file defines (nerves, screens) have numbers and answer as the headers' classes do (1.3)
capabilities.services.registry: Services by name and version: bound at import, the minor rule, optional imports, a table's size, mistakes reported once a place and counted (2.1)
capabilities.services.events: Events posted from any thread, given on the game thread at the frame's start in list order, 256 a frame, none after a mod's stop (2.1)
capabilities.services.permissions: A permissioned service bound only when the player granted its permission; asked for by name, refused and said (2.1)
capabilities.services.time: The world clock: frames and world steps, a rate from 1 to 16000 thousandths, hold and single steps, the game's sound following (2.2)
capabilities.services.time.timers: Timers on frames, world steps or real nanoseconds, given as events, cancelled exactly (2.2)
capabilities.services.time.handlers: Frame and step handlers in list order, every world step its own call (2.2)
capabilities.services.time.real: The monotonic clock from any thread and the wall clock with the player's offset (2.2)
capabilities.script.build: A LumaScript mod compiled by LumaLink to the platform's machine code (C with #line markers, clang), loaded by the game like any luma.h mod; its hooks run and its facts reach the harness (4.3)
capabilities.services.system: Facts of the platform, the game and the player's locale; the game window's display (2.2)
capabilities.services.system.clipboard: The system clipboard, text and RGBA images, read and written as requests, the window in front (2.2)
capabilities.services.system.links: A https link opened in the browser, one at a time, 10 s apart, a Note naming its site (2.2)
capabilities.consent.screen: Before a mod's code first runs the player is asked, on a screen naming the mod and each permission with its why; nothing runs until the answer (6.4)
capabilities.consent.allow: Allow starts the mod's code with the permissions granted, kept for the next start (6.4)
capabilities.consent.notnow: Not now, Escape or B: the mod's code stays off and the page does not ask again this run (6.4)
capabilities.consent.choose: Choose grants permissions one by one; a required one not allowed keeps the code off, said on its row (6.4)
capabilities.consent.nocode: A mod with no code for this platform is never asked, whatever permissions it declares (6.4)
capabilities.modlog.nocost: With no mod the log's store is never made: no notice, no entry, no fact (3.12)
capabilities.modlog.validator: A mod the check refuses has its reason as an entry by code, file and line, the validator's words kept in English (3.12)
capabilities.validator.start: Each start every placed package goes through the one validator; its findings are entries in the mod log, Notes as Notes (validator 2)
capabilities.validator.start.refuse: A package the start's check finds an Error in does not start; the Mods page says its log says why (validator 2)
capabilities.import.check: A mod imported (a drop, the picker, Open with) goes through the one validator before it is placed; the result page shows what happened and its findings (validator 2 at import, 6.1)
capabilities.import.refuse: A package the import's check finds an Error in is not placed: NOT IMPORTED, its findings listed (6.1)
capabilities.import.against_placed: The import's check reads the placed packages, so a need on no list refuses it (6.1)
capabilities.import.already: A mod imported that is already in the mods folder unchanged is neither added nor replaced: ALREADY IN YOUR MODS (6.1)
capabilities.import.takes_over: A mod whose takes_over names an id no installed mod has is imported with the line Takes over what {old} kept under it, as a fact (services-save 6, 6.5)
capabilities.modscreen.list: Each mod's line in the Mods tab's lists is the fact modscreen.<id> as shown, written once while it does not change (harness 4, 6.2)
capabilities.modscreen.page: Each row of a mod's page is the fact modscreen.<id> as shown, each time the page opens (harness 4, 6.2)
capabilities.controls.mod_actions: CONTROLS lists each running mod's input actions after the game's bindings, by name, each following its game control until bound; Enter and an input bind one per scheme, applied with the page and kept in the settings (2.5 layer 1b, 6.3)
capabilities.modscreen.code_time: A mod's page shows CODE TIME, its code's time a frame over its last 120 frames from the guard's luma_guard_cost (6.7, guard 3b)
capabilities.mods.safe_start: A safe start (--safe-start 1, Shift at the start) plans every mod off for that start and keeps the player's choices; the Mods tab says so (6.6)
capabilities.mods.safe_start.crash: After a crash with mods on the next start is safe by itself and the Mods tab says why; the start after is not (6.6)
capabilities.mods.blocklist: BLOCK on a mod's page turns it off and keeps it off at every start, whatever the player's choices say, until UNBLOCK on its page (6.6)
capabilities.validator.start.kept: A package unchanged since the last start (names, sizes, times, then content) is not validated again: its kept findings are read back (validator 2)
capabilities.modlog.text: Entries shown in the player's language with the language's font (3.12)
capabilities.modlog.keep: One entry a (file, line, code): repeats are counted on it, never new lines (3.12)
capabilities.modlog.notice: Errors while playing show at most three notices, newest at the bottom; the rest wait their turn (3.12)
capabilities.modlog.notice.fold: Notices waiting beyond the room fold into one line saying how many more (3.12)
capabilities.modlog.notice.summary: Errors at start bring one summary notice at the title, naming how many (3.12)
capabilities.modlog.limits: At most 256 entries a mod and 1,024 a session; past them one line says how many were not kept (3.12)
capabilities.modlog.threads: The same cause from another thread and the game thread is one entry, counted (3.12)
capabilities.modlog.page: Mods > Log lists each mod's entries with place and count, reached by pad and keys (3.12)
capabilities.modlog.entry: An entry opens whole: its source, its place and all its text, in pages (3.12)
capabilities.refs.nocost: With no mod the references check is never called and no placeholder is made (3.12)
capabilities.startcheck.part: A game part missing (the shader compiler) is said in one line naming it (3.13)
capabilities.startcheck.allmodsoff: With a game part missing every mod is off and the title is still reached (3.13)
capabilities.startcheck.nocost: With no mod none of the game's parts is checked: no line, no notice (3.13)
capabilities.fx.particle_missing: A particle name an effect lists that no resource has is said once by name, in the mod's log when it is a mod's, and the game goes on (3.5)
capabilities.effects.no_resource_slot: An effect's emitter whose particle is missing keeps its place in the effect's list and is never made; the others play (3.5)
capabilities.fx.start: content.fx start: a game particle on an actor at a joint, followed, shows particles; the handle is the mod's (3.5)
capabilities.fx.stop: content.fx stop ends the handle (fading or at once); an ended handle is refused (3.5)
capabilities.fx.missing: A name in no store: the placeholder, LUMA_OK, Content.MissingEffect once per name (3.5)
capabilities.fx.joint: A joint the actor lacks: the base, LUMA_OK, Content.MissingJoint once (3.5)
capabilities.fx.refusals: content.fx refuses a null, dead or wrong actor, an empty name, a null out, a short LumaPlace, a bad scale and unknown handles, each reported, nothing written (3.5)
capabilities.fx.place: content.fx places an effect by offset and turn, left where it started, tinted by scale and colour (3.5)
capabilities.fx.alive: The harness's fx.alive facts follow a handle for its first frames only (3.5)
capabilities.fx.nocost: With no mod nothing of content.fx runs: no fx facts (3.5)
capabilities.fx.limit: content.fx keeps 256 open effects a mod; the 257th is LUMA_E_LIMIT, reported once; a stopped one frees its place (3.5)
capabilities.fx.on_model: content.fx starts an effect on a model the mod attached, at its joint, and ends it with the model (3.5)
capabilities.fx.replace: A mod's effects.json replaces a game particle the game's own table starts, with no code: the cook keeps its number and says so (cook.effect) (3.5, effects 7)
capabilities.fx.group: A mod's own effect of several emitters takes its source's draw group: cooked into its effects list, started with every emitter in that group (3.5, effects 4)
capabilities.fx.actor_end: An effect on an actor that dies ends with it ("actor"), as the actor's own effects; the ended handle and a start on the dead actor are refused (3.5)
capabilities.model.attach: content.model attaches a game model to an actor, drawn as the game draws its own (3.2)
capabilities.model.joint_follow: An attached model follows one joint of its actor every frame (3.2)
capabilities.model.missing: A model in no store: the placeholder model, LUMA_OK, Content.MissingModel counted (3.2)
capabilities.model.missing_joint: A joint the actor lacks: the base, LUMA_OK, Content.MissingJoint once (3.2)
capabilities.model.refusals: content.model's refusals answer their status and write no handle (3.2)
capabilities.model.skeleton_follow: An attached model's joints take the actor's joints of their names every frame (3.2)
capabilities.model.place: An attached model is placed by offset and turn from what it follows (3.2)
capabilities.model.show: An attached model is hidden and shown by the mod (3.2)
capabilities.model.detach: detach ends the handle; an ended handle answers LUMA_E_HANDLE (3.2)
capabilities.model.reuse: A detached model's part is used again for the same actor, model and follow (3.2)
capabilities.model.limit: content.model refuses a mod's attach past LUMA_CONTENT_MODEL_MOST open ones; a detach frees one (3.2)
capabilities.ui.mod_layout: ui opens a mod's own cooked layout (<Name>.layout.json, 3.8 layer 1): its picture and text panes drawn by the game's layout drawer, its text set by name (3.8 layer 1)
capabilities.ui.open: ui opens a screen layout (the game's or the mod's cooked one) on the HUD, drawn by the game's layout drawer every frame (2.4 layer 4, 3.8 layer 1)
capabilities.ui.pane: ui finds a pane of an open screen by its exact name; the same pane is the same handle (2.4, 3.8)
capabilities.ui.text: ui sets a text pane's text from UTF-8, kept as given in every script (2.4, 3.8)
capabilities.ui.text_cut: A text longer than its pane holds is cut there, LUMA_OK, Ui.TextCut said (2.4, 3.8)
capabilities.ui.visible: ui shows and hides a pane and a whole screen (2.4, 3.8)
capabilities.ui.refusals: ui's refusals answer their status and write no handle; close ends a screen and its panes (2.4, 3.8)
capabilities.ui.reuse: A screen a mod closed is that mod's again when it opens the layout on the layer: its panes shown as the layout has them (2.4, 3.8)
capabilities.ui.limit: ui refuses a mod's open past LUMA_UI_MOST_SCREENS open ones; a close frees one (2.4, 3.8)
capabilities.ui.play: ui plays a layout animation on a screen, once or looping, whatever its data says (2.4, 3.8 layer 3)
capabilities.ui.animation_end: A played animation's end comes as LUMA_UI_EVENT_ANIMATION_END at a frame's start: LUMA_OK at its end, LUMA_E_CANCELLED when stopped first (2.4, 3.8)
capabilities.anim.play: anim plays a clip of a game actor's model: every kind of that name started as the game starts its own, the first leading (3.6 run time)
capabilities.anim.on_model: anim plays a mod model's own glTF clips on the model the mod attached (3.6 run time)
capabilities.anim.how: A play's rate, start frame, once or loop and blend are the mod's, whatever the clip says (3.6 run time)
capabilities.anim.mark: A play's marks come as LUMA_ANIM_EVENT_MARK each time the clip passes them, every loop (3.6 run time)
capabilities.anim.end: A once clip's end comes as LUMA_ANIM_EVENT_END LUMA_OK; stop, another play, detach give LUMA_E_CANCELLED with the why (3.6 run time)
capabilities.anim.frame: anim reads a play's frame and its clip's last frame (3.6 run time)
capabilities.anim.refusals: anim's refusals answer their status and write no handle; a missing clip is Content.MissingAnimation (3.6 run time)
capabilities.anim.events: A clip's own events (its <clip>.anim.json, cooked to <clip>.events beside it) come to a play as marks after the mod's own, each with its name (anim 1.1, 3.6 layer 3)
capabilities.anim.game_clip: A clip a mod's animation file replaced is the one the game plays and anim plays (3.6 layer 2 and run time)
capabilities.model.scene_end: A model on an actor the scene releases ends "scene" once at the release, and nothing of it is touched after (models 7)
capabilities.model.actor_end: A model on an actor that dies ends "actor" once, as the actor's own parts; the ended handle and an attach on the dead actor are refused (3.2)
capabilities.model.player_parts: content.model lists the player's parts and the joints they are drawn at (3.2)
capabilities.services.mods: The session's list of mods: order, id, name, version, kind, code, and state as the player and the check left it (2.2)
capabilities.services.mods.ids: Numbers in the game's message and sensor spaces by <mod id>/<name>, derived alike on every machine, kept and never reused (2.2)
capabilities.services.mods.install: A mod's request to install a .luma through the import screen and the player's answer (2.2)
capabilities.services.save: A mod's own values in the player's game file: written when the game saves, copied and erased with the file, per character (2.2)
capabilities.services.save.global: A mod's values across files, written at once (2.2)
capabilities.services.save.game: The game's own file handed to a mod, or offered back through the game's screen with the player's answer (2.2)
capabilities.services.fs: A mod's data folder and its own installed files: read, written whole, removed, moved, listed, the same path rule everywhere (2.3)
capabilities.services.fs.exchange: The Exchange folder shared by the player and mods granted it (2.3)
capabilities.services.net.local: TCP on this machine and the local network: connect, listen, send, take, close (2.7 layer 1)
capabilities.services.net.internet: TCP to the hosts luma.json names, by name or address, public addresses only: connect, send, take, close (2.7 layer 2)
capabilities.services.net.udp: UDP datagrams (1.1 of net.local and net.internet): udp_open, udp_connect, send_to, take_datagram, DATAGRAM (2.7 layer 2b)
capabilities.services.assets: The game's files by path as the game reads them, mods' over the game's or the game's own: find, bytes, a folder's entries (2.8 layer 1)
capabilities.services.input: A mod's own actions (its luma.json key options), each following a game control until the player binds keys or buttons to it in Controls, read each game frame (2.5)
